Fixed bug in R2016a parsing of text properties

Compatibility with all the Matlab releases, which have been slowly
rolling out new legend objects and syntax between R2014b and R2016a
(with various bugs mixed in), is getting tricky.

Thus far I'm continuing to rely on the legacy version of legend
(make_legend with version='on'),
which creates an axis object, rather than a legend object.  Despite
my best attempts, and dives into the undocumented properties of the
new legend objects, I haven't found a good way to access and alter
the legend object's child text and plot marker objects.

In R2016a, the legacy version of the legend command introduces a bug
where text properties (such as font size and interpreter)
are not properly applied to the legend text.  This update includes
a workaround for this bug.

I also updated the input parsing to use the newer addParameter
inputParser method, instead of addParamValue.

Added 'Biomass' to the potential pedigree table column headings

In EwE6, the biomass pedigree value is usually labeled BiomassAreaInput.
However, in an older model updated from EwE5 .mdb format to EwE6 .ewemdb
format, I found some columns labeled as simply 'Biomass'.  Pretty sure
this is just a legacy artifact, and I'm treating these values the same
as those marked as BiomassAreaInput.

Finalized update related to upper tail end of stanza B/QB curves

Finally tracked down the source of small discrepancies in B/QB between
my code and the EwE6 code.  EwE6 uses a 90% Winf value as the upper
bound for monthly calcs, then adds an accumulator function to deal
with the extra biomass/consumption in the last month.  I insted just
use 99.99% Winf as the upper bound.  Close enough, and doesn't add much
extra computation time since I don't loop over months, just need to use
slightly larger matrices.  No big code changes needed to resolve this one,
so I just updated the documentation to explain this.

Changed amax to 90%, plus minor bug fix

I changed the code so that it now uses a 90% age as the upper month for
the oldest stanza group, rather than the 99% limit I had been using.  This
is just to maintain consistency with both EwE and Rpath.

Also, fixed bug where I had inconsistent use of the bab variable.

Added landings and discards to pedigree matrix

Landings and discards can now be assigned a pedigree value.  If not included,
should be assumed to be constant, so should be back-compatible.

Corrected DC transpose bug

When replicating DC pedigree value across all prey groups, I had a small typo
that accidentally applied the values to all predator-prey values  with the target
group as prey rather than as predator.  In experiments where all diet pedigree
values were the same (luckily, my published studies) this bug would have no affect,
but when applying different values, or more importantly, trying to vary diet value
for only one or two groups in isolation, this could lead to the wrong parameters
being varied.  Bug now corrected.
Added more robust check for whether multi-stanza groups are present

Code overhaul for clarity and flexibility

Calculations are unchanged, but code overhauled in several ways:

- Made the plot flag an input variable (previously hardcoded off)
- Added discretization interval as an input parameter (previously
  hardcoded to one month)
- Main calculations moved into a subfunction
- Simplified plots to no longer rely on external functions

Also, BAB parameter can now be a vector, as in RPath, or a scalar,
as in EwE6.

Now skips vertical alignment fix if title added

In the previous update, I added some adjustments to the y-position of
objects to try to account for some Tex/LaTeX issues.  However, that fix
doesn't work if a title is included for the legend.  For now, just skipping
over the adjustments if title is included; will have to add the correct
adjustments when I get some time.

Added workaround for vertical alignment issues

I addd in some code to reposition text vertically.  This will hopefully solve
some of the issues seen with tex and latex legend labels.  In my tests it works
pretty well for LaTeX text, but is hit or miss for TeX (no worse than the old
version though, so might as well try).  Thanks to Søren Enemark for the
suggested workaround.

Added nolisten parameter to legendflex.m

I still haven't figured out a great way to get the labeled-object listeners
to update efficiently when multiple objects are updated at once.  This can
cause some major slowdowns when updating large numbers of objects, including
when printing to file.  As a workaround, I'm adding the option to remove
these listeners.

Changed default ncol/nrow value from NaN to 0

In previous versions, if the default value for nrow/ncol input was passed
in manually, the NaN value would fail the integer validation check.  I
hadn't originally intended a user to manually pass that, but it's perfectly
reasonable to assume they might (for code consistency reasons), so I've
changed the default value to 0.  The value still means "as many as necessary".
Merging updates from ecopathlite subtree

Corrected bug in listeners when legend deleted; hggroup issue discovered.

I corrected a bug where the callback that resyncs the legend to the labeled
objects would cause an error if the user manually deleted the legend.  It now
verifies that the legend exists before running the listener callbacks.

Also, a user alerted me to a bug that occurs if one attempts to label an hggroup
object in R2014b+.  For some reason, the legend line/patch/etc objects have an
empty Tag property, rather than being labeled with the appropriate legend text.
I use those tags to figure out which symbols go where, so for now I do not have
a workaround for that, except to advise users not to pass hggroup objects to
legendflex.

Corrected a few typos in Algorithm 5

Forgot to pass the islive variable to the subfunction; also, minor logic
flaw when checking for failure to fill unknowns (only worked for multi-ensemble
case).  Both errors have been corrected.

Overhauled legendflex for better compatibility with HG2 graphics

In this update, I've made some major changes to the code so that it is
now compatibile with both old and new (post-R2014b) handle graphics.  Now the same
function can be run in any version of Matlab, rather than needing two functions
(which had been my stopgap solution since the release of R2014b).  Primary changes
involved replacing the old resize function with individual listeners to keep
the legend in sync with changing axes positions and labeled-object properties, and
updating the preallocation of handles as either numerics or graphics objects as
appropriate to version.

The contour-labeling bug is still present as of R2015a-beta... will need to keep
an eye on this as new releases come out.
